title: Certify the sharp recursive-size window of Gaussian residue recovery
body:
PR3881 supplies a paid exact-residue multiplication to lower Gaussian recovery precision. This package determines exactly when that child is strictly smaller than the declared parent width, including partially filled top digits, and executes the new boundary point. **No new κ, physical caller or whole-cost improvement is claimed.**

For the unchanged 455-point source box and 64-bit digits:

- At the full 14,592-bit width, the largest admitted residue width is **k=28, p=180**, with **14,556-bit** child inputs. At k=29 the maximal input attains **15,011-bit** children, so strict shrinkage fails.
- **k=27** is the largest fixed width that works throughout its entire supported tail, n=28..14,592. k=28 has explicitly classified holes above 8,192 bits.
- The sharp formula is `min(k,t)+(L−1)(2k+ceil(log₂ L))`, where L=ceil(n/64) and t is the top digit width. It finds **599 admissible pairs missed by the conservative bound**; the unchanged predecessor’s conservative receipt remains correct. An actual n=65/k=29 execution has 60-bit children despite its conservative 88-bit bound.

The written proof covers general positive n,b and source-admitted k, with an attaining all-ones input. Exact arithmetic certifies p_min=208−k for all k=0..64 **for this frozen sufficient certificate**. The all-input finite-box implication retains the predecessor’s numerical/backend proof premises.

**Validation:** all 933,888 fixed-box (n,k) pairs checked by two separately implemented engines; 70 independent literal packed-word witnesses; three freshly regenerated p=180 operator certificates/matrices; two complete maximal-input Gaussian products; 12 real CLI negative controls and two positive controls under normal/optimized Python. Python 3.12 registered replay passed (20.86 s, maximum child RSS 75,497,472 bytes); a regular-only, read-only, inode-disjoint Git-free export passed all three commands. Commit-byte and scoped diff checks passed. No fresh Lean/native/selected-supplier cold replay is claimed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-residue-shrink-window`.

Credit **Dugongue** for PR3881 at `75e098dc12a2567e73a2858137408e08d31dbf84`, **Mason Hale** for the certified Gaussian backend, and their retained source notices for earlier contributors. Jose Manuel’s PR3878 is physical-caller context only. New work by ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate AI arithmetic verification and mathematical review; no independent human or formal-kernel review.

Remaining obligations: actual physical tensor/CRT/residue composition, the complete paid cost inequality, and an all-size recurrence/basecase policy. Q=448 enclosure arithmetic is unchanged. PR3890, upstream sources and the selected frontier are preserved. Base refreshed at main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision6; live overlap rechecked before publication.


Task: `independent-moment`, scope **refined** to a concrete recursive-size interface (seed `95c2f6780dcb30b8ecca22b24e893a81`); the proposed formal/chronology checks were already covered.
